doc.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 29, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Centerpiece, knowing where you are, and singing with Jon Hendricks
summary: Gates discusses getting in front of the beat and singing Centerpiece with Jon Hendricks and Company.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Right. Okay. Name this tune, you ready? [hums “Centerpiece”].
[sings] The more I feel my love increase. “Centerpiece.”
Okay. So here’s what you did with —

Singers get behind, not many get in front. But I just kind of heard it that way. And if I work with a rhythm section where I’ve never worked with and I tell them I’m going to do that and maybe I’ll open with that, I’ll tell them, “listen, I know where I am. You know, you cats just play the map, I know where I am.” Because lots of times they’ll adjust, “uh oh, he doesn’t know where he is.” The singer. That’s a singer thing. “Oh the singer’s lost, let’s adjust.” Well they should. But they should tell the singer, say, “listen, we had to adjust to you baby, because you were out of whack.” “Oh really?” Because some don’t know that. But the piano player will never tell the singer because the singer might get an attitude. So I let them know, I know where I am. You don’t have to adjust. We’ll meet back up again and then I’m going to let you go and then I’ll catch you again. And they’ll go, “solid.” In fact, I had a wonderful opportunity to sing a few times with Jon Hendricks, Aria Hendricks and Kevin Burke, when it was Lambert, Hendricks, uh, Jon Hendricks and Company. And they said, “come on up here, man.” And they were going to do “Centerpiece.” And I got like — like instead of singing in the harmony, because they’re great with their harmonies. I let them sing in their harmony and I was kind of like around it somewhere. And Jon looked at me and grinned. And that made me feel like all right, I’m in now. You know?
Yeah. A grin from Jon Hendricks.
